component.name: Tether
component.summary: Your Android phone on your desktop

description.p: Tether puts your Android phone on your Linux desktop. Text from your computer, see and answer phone notifications, and open your phone's apps in their own windows. It works on any desktop, including GNOME, KDE Plasma, Sway and i3.
On the phone you use the free KDE Connect app. Tether is the computer side.

ul.li: Messages: your conversations with names from your contacts, picture messages, and a copy button for one-time codes
Phone apps in their own windows, set up by scanning one QR code
Notifications from the phone, with replies and actions
Clipboard shared both ways, files and links sent by dropping them on the window
What plays on the phone, on your keyboard's media keys
Ring your phone to find it, and ring the computer from the phone
Browse the phone's files, search its contacts, and type on the phone from the computer's keyboard
Use the phone as a touchpad, keyboard and presentation remote, and to lock the screen, change the volume, control music and run commands you set up

description.p: Everything KDE Connect does, in both directions. The phone can now control this computer: touchpad and keyboard, presentation remote, lock, volume, music on the computer, ringing the computer, and commands you set up. New Files, Contacts, Keyboard and Devices pages, this computer's notifications on the phone (if you turn it on), music that pauses during calls, complete file sharing with progress, discovery on networks that block broadcasts, and a checklist of what to switch on in the phone app.
A Settings screen, and a tray icon that shows how many conversations are unread and opens the window with a click.

A Photos page with the newest camera photos and screenshots from your phone, Copy and Save on screenshot notifications, conversations that are there as soon as the window opens, and a window that stays quick with hundreds of conversations.
After pairing phone apps, Tether now reaches the phone even when the network hides its announcements, and reconnects to it on its own later.
Phone-app pairing finds the phone on more networks, pairing by code takes only the 6 digits, and a new version replaces the old background service right away.
Updates itself. Phone-app pairing finds the phone even when the network blocks the usual discovery, and pairing by code needs only the 6 digits.
Phone apps in their own windows, set up by scanning a QR code. Pin phone apps to the computer's app menu. Safer pairing and file transfers.
First release: messages, notifications, clipboard, files and media controls.
